chapter: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
title: Strolling without a pianist, and Ike Quebec joins the group
summary: They played piano-less; Ike Quebec joined and it became one of the best bandstand feelings of his career.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So we strolled for two nights, and we had one more night before the week was ended. We'd have a day off. The -- not the week wasn't ended, but that was the day our day off would fall on. So the owner, manager, proprietor, Al Barnes, he gave Charlie the day off to go into Chicago and get another piano player. So he gave us a bottle of Seagram's V.O. to take on the train with us, because he had been gracious enough to keep us furnished at the club. He wanted us to have a good trip, you know? So, while Charlie was buying the tickets, I said, well, Ike, let's go into the commissary and some sandwiches.
Ike Quebec had joined us later and augmented the group.
Which made it sound, oh, too tough. I mean, I'm just only sorry that we didn't record that group.
It was during the first week that Ike Quebec joined you.
